prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: 2 by 2 production plate with FOUR equal SQUARE same-camera scene states for a Mars game. Image 1 supplies the exact recognizable cream lander identity, teal circular hatch, angular dark windows, roof tanks, ladder and substantial splayed leg struts. Image 2 is only a reference for two separate lander filling ports; DISCARD all its foreground plant, tanks, solar panels and ceramic platforms. Reframe close on the lander and two PORTABLE locally made IRON GAS CYLINDERS. No processing factory anywhere, no solar panels anywhere, no reactor or cryogenic stores. No habitat needed in this closer view. All four states have exactly the same camera, scenery, lander and bottle positions.
Common scene: the complete same lander stands upper-middle on orange rocky ground, occupying about 65 percent of panel width. Under the low crossmember just RIGHT of its ladder, a SHORT substantial dull-Iron tubular support with saddle/base rests on a low ceramic footer between two low ceramic side blocking stacks. This short support is about the diameter of an original lander strut and does not raise the cabin. NO catch rock. Foreground left is one small plain robust dull-Iron O2 cylinder with a tiny blue service collar, reused compact valve, rounded shoulder, flat stable foot and carrying collar. Foreground right is its matching CH4 cylinder with a tiny ochre service collar. Each bottle is only about one fifth of the spacecraft height, genuinely portable, simple and solid, not insulated or frosted, not in a cage, no huge foundation. Small legible stencils O2 and CH4 identify them. Two dedicated dark flexible service hoses lie neatly beside their own bottles when disconnected.
TOP LEFT: both cylinders present, both hoses DISCONNECTED and loosely coiled near their matching bottles; lander has an accessible small LEFT fill port beside hatch and small RIGHT fill port beside hatch.
TOP RIGHT: left O2 bottle connects by ONE continuous hose from its own valve to the lander's LEFT port. Right CH4 bottle remains disconnected, its hose coiled beside it.
BOTTOM LEFT: right CH4 bottle connects by ONE continuous hose from its valve to the RIGHT port. Left O2 bottle remains disconnected, its hose coiled beside it.
BOTTOM RIGHT: both of those separate complete hoses connected; neither line joins the other. Keep full routes legible without covering hatch/ladder or small repaired support. Bottle positions and proportions identical across every panel.
Style: exact warm cream/teal retro industrial expedition family from references, believable matte iron and rubber, softly painted detailed scientific story illustration, warm upper-left Mars sunlight. Two equal columns, two equal rows, no gutters, panels borders, titles, people, diagram arrows or captions. Do not inherit source image's two huge factory tanks, pads or panels.
